info.title: API.SH: The Numbers
info.description: The The Numbers API from API.SH: public The Numbers data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

tags.description: Your balance, usage, logs and past responses. Free.

401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

get.summary: Your calls of the last 30 days
get.description: Newest first. Filter by status, route prefix, key or time; page with `before` (the `next` value). Add output=csv|ndjson to download (up to 5,000 rows per request; the next cursor is in the x-next-cursor header). Free.

get.summary: Fetch a past response again, free
get.description: The exact response a call returned, for 30 days after the call, at no cost. Use the call's x-request-id. Supports output=csv|ndjson.

200.description: The stored response (headers: x-refetch: 1, x-original-time, x-original-route).

404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

get.description:
The daily domestic chart: rank, previous rank, title, gross, changes, theaters, theater average, total gross, days or weeks in release. Each row carries every column the site shows, named after its header (money, counts and changes as numbers), with the movie id (for `/thenumbers/v1/movie`) and ISO dates next to the column they come from. Without a date, the latest day.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/thenumbers-daily

parameters.name: days_ago
parameters.description: The chart this many days before today (instead of date).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.name: Daily Domestic Box Office Chart for Saturday, November 1, 2025

get.summary: A franchise's movies with budgets and grosses
get.description:
Every movie of a franchise: release date, title, movie id, production budget, opening weekend, domestic and worldwide box office.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/thenumbers-franchise

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The franchise part of a the-numbers.com/movies/franchise/ link (`Star-Wars`) or the link.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.name: Star Wars Franchise Box Office History

get.summary: Movie box office, budget, details, performance, territories, cast and crew
get.description:
One movie: synopsis; domestic, international and worldwide box office and video sales; metrics (opening weekend and share, legs, domestic share, production budget, theater counts, inflation-adjusted gross); details (domestic and international releases, video release, MPA rating, running time, franchise, keywords, source, genre, production method, creative type, production companies, countries, languages); weekend, daily and weekly performance; box office per international territory; leading, supporting and cameo cast with roles; production and technical credits.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/thenumbers-movie

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The movie part of a the-numbers.com link (`Avatar-(2009)`) or the link itself; ids come with every chart and search row.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Box office records: all-time and per release year, domestic, international, worldwide
get.description:
Record charts (top 100): all-time or per release year cumulative grosses for domestic, international or worldwide box office (with release date, distributor or biggest territory, genre, tickets sold), or the biggest single days at the domestic box office (`measure=daily`). Each row carries every column the site shows, named after its header (money, counts and changes as numbers), with the movie id (for `/thenumbers/v1/movie`) and ISO dates next to the column they come from.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/thenumbers-records

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Top-grossing leading stars at the worldwide box office
get.description:
Leading actors ranked by the worldwide box office of their films, 100 a page: rank, name, worldwide box office, number of movies and average per movie. Pass `next_offset` back as `offset`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/thenumbers-stars

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Row offset, a multiple of 100 (from next_offset).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.name: Top 100 Stars in Leading Roles at the Worldwide Box Office

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
